question: The Indian telecom sector was liberalised under which year’s Telecom Policy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1994**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian telecom sector was liberalized under the **National Telecom Policy of 1994**.
 
• The policy introduced **private sector participation** in providing telecom services, which was earlier monopolized by the government.
 
• It aimed to **increase tele-density** and improve the quality of services by allowing private players to operate in the telecom space.
 
• The 1994 policy laid the groundwork for further liberalization and reforms, including the entry of private companies in the telecom sector.
 
• This reform was a major step towards **modernizing India's telecom infrastructure** and ensuring widespread connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI):** Established in 1997, TRAI is responsible for regulating telecom services, including tariffs and ensuring fair competition.
 
• **Subsequent Policies:** The 1999 New Telecom Policy (NTP) further liberalized the sector and introduced revenue-sharing models instead of fixed license fees.
 
• **Telecom Revolution:** The liberalization and reforms of the 1990s paved the way for the telecom revolution in India, with rapid growth in mobile phone penetration and internet services.
 
• **FDI in Telecom:** The sector has also attracted significant foreign direct investment (FDI), with the government allowing up to 100% FDI in certain areas.
 
• **Impact:** Today, India is one of the largest telecom markets globally, with billions of subscribers and a robust digital infrastructure.
